assertions.name: bar_decomposition_sums_to_total_at_q_proton
assertions.source: Δtr_M(q) = sym + antisym by linearity of bar-involution

description: Structural observation: Δtr_M(q) bar-decomposition under q → 1/q. Records the closed forms of the symmetric and antisymmetric components without proposing a c_k closure candidate (per AGENTS.md no-7th-ansatz discipline).

data.structural_finding: Δtr_M(q) decomposes in t = q^(1/2) as sym(t) + antisym(t) under t ↔ 1/t. The symmetric part has a clean closed form (see sym_part_t_factored); the antisymmetric part is more intricate. This decomposition is the natural projection onto bar-eigenspaces of the Hecke bar-involution.
data.anti_pattern_guard: This probe does NOT propose a c_k closure. Any future attempt to use this decomposition for c_k must pass the cross-anchor test (q_proton vs q_muon) AND have a structural justification — not just numerical near-match.
data.follow_up_research_direction: (NEW) Decomposing Q_β candidate forms onto bar-symmetric / antisymmetric projections may give a structured attack on the Habiro element identification. The sym part is in the binding (Li_2^q) sector per prop:li2q-phiq-bar-symmetrization; the antisym part is in the mass (Φ_q) sector. Q_β being a mass DIFFERENCE means the sym projection is dominant — investigating which Wedderburn blocks contribute to sym vs antisym could narrow the Habiro search.
